questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere English speaking with a nice climate and beautiful surroundings

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend Vancouver and UBC to anyone going on exchange, it is a great campus and a beautiful city!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The go global office was only available to contact through zoom in the beginning of the term, but it was still relatively easy to get answers to any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got help changing my course registrations.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many different dorms, both studios and shared apartments

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had my own kitchen in my studio

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I chose a few different dorms in a prioritized list, but in the end I was offered a different (and much more expensive) room, and I had to either accept it or not live on campus, which was a bit annoying. I think it was really worth it to avoid commuting to campus, though. Also, it seemed like it was relatively easy to switch apartments after arriving (e.g. from a studio to a shared apartment or vice versa)
In my dorm there were almost exclusively exchange students, and a LOT of danish people, so maybe not the best option for meeting canadians.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It wasn't too difficult, just a lot of work. And because there are no course descriptions available online, it was also a bit of work to get the KU pre-approval

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I filled out a list of 10 courses a long time before the term started, and I was then registered in some of them. It is possible to add and drop courses two weeks into the term, so it is pretty easy to get the courses you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The go global office handled my course changes after the term started, which was nice. That way I was sure I was doing it right.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I pretty much got the courses I wanted, I changed them a little around after I tried the courses I was registered for initially.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try the courses out and make sure to change them if you feel like it. Some courses have crazy workloads for no real reason, and it's not worth spending all your time on exchange doing endless assignments.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one 300 level and two 400 level courses, and the level was about the same as I would expect at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very different in the different courses. In general there are more little homework assignments during the term, and especially in the smaller courses (<50 students) some participation was expected and graded.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MICB 325 Analysis of Microbial Genes and Genomes
MICB 418 Industrial Microbiology and Biotechnology
MICB 425 Microbial Ecological Genomics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all the courses, basically. 325 and 418 overlapped a bit with courses I had taken at home, so they were on the easier side. They were both more lecture-based with homework questions through the term. 425 had a more philosophical take on ecological microbiology and then transitioned to a more practical data science approach and had a group project in the end.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The dorm I was offered was very expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food in supermarkets was very expensive, eating out was pretty cheap (especially sushi, hehe).
Staying in hotels was very expensive, which made it very expensive to stay in the Vancouver area after the term ended.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not that much was going on, but I think that was due to the campus being partly shut down due to the pandemic for the first few weeks of the term. After that, there was more activity, but I think there could be more.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of athletic opportunities, and many of them were free or cheap for students. Things like the aquatic centre, the recreation centre (sports, dance and yoga classes, fitness etc.) and many other facilities were fun to explore.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The hot tub in the aquatic centre, and the museums on campus are free to students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes, there are many opportunities around north and west vancouver that are accessible with bus. Also exploring some of the more quiet neighbourhoods in vancouver, like the west side or burnaby.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, vancouver is a very international city, so people are very used to many different cultures being mixed

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Come when there isn't a pandemic lol

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very nice and polite, and open to talking to new people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The spring term ends really early, so you can travel for a month after the term and still have a full summer back home if you want. Vancouver is maybe even more gorgeous in real life than in pictures, and the weather is way better there than in all other places in Canada. Although a rainjacket and some waterproof shoes are essential.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having an everyday life in a different city so far from home and meeting lots of new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The term overlapped with the KU term in the beginning, which made the workload in the first month pretty hard. Also it can be a bit hard to talk to people at home due to the nine hour time difference.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
